case.question: What are the three main methods to clear a fault on the GS10 drive, and which method is the safest in a production environment?

key_points: Method 1: Press the Stop button on the keypad or set control mode to Manual, then address the fault condition and restart
Method 2: Cycle the drive power completely OFF then back ON after confirming the fault condition has been corrected and load is secured
Method 3: Use a digital input terminal (e.g., terminal block inputs used for fault clear command via drive configuration) to signal fault clear after root cause is addressed
The safest method in production is Method 2 (power cycle) after confirming the fault condition has been corrected and the motor load is secured
wrong_if: States that only the keypad method is safe; all three are valid when used correctly in appropriate contexts
Recommends power-cycling the drive immediately during active motor operation to clear a fault
Claims that digital input fault clear commands bypass the need to address root causes before clearing
Suggests any single button press will clear a fault within seconds without addressing the underlying problem

turns.question: What are the three main methods to clear a fault on the GS10 drive, and which method is the safest in a production environment?
turns.answer: The loaded GS10 excerpts do not give three universal fault-clear methods for the drive, so I can only point to the ones shown: manual reset with the keypad R key for EF faults [5], and STO faults auto-reset when P06.44=1 after the STO error is cleared or can be reset manually when P06.44=0 [3]. If you want the safest production choice, send the full fault/clear section or the specific fault code so I can answer from the manual exactly.
